views.name: film_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  film_id,
  title,
  description,
  release_year,
  language_id,
  original_language_id,
  rental_duration,
  rental_rate,
  length,
  replacement_cost,
  rating,
  special_features,
  last_update
FROM film
views.description: Normalized one-row-per-film projection exposing core film attributes and measures. Use this as the canonical film dimension for joins and aggregations (keeps numeric measures as-is to allow sums/averages). | Use for: Film-level reports (counts, averages, filtering by attributes like rating/language/release_year); Joins to categories, actors, inventory, and rentals for downstream analysis

views.name: actor_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  actor_id,
  first_name,
  last_name,
  last_update
FROM actor
views.description: One-row-per-actor projection including identifiers and name parts. Useful for joining actor attributes into film/credit analyses. | Use for: Actor counts per film, actor search by name, actor-level aggregates

views.name: customer_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  store_id,
  first_name,
  last_name,
  email,
  address_id,
  active,
  create_date,
  last_update
FROM customer
views.description: One-row-per-customer projection with contact and status fields. Use for customer-level joins and cohorting by create_date/active/store. | Use for: Customer lifetime value, active customer cohorts, joins to rental/payment history

views.name: inventory_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  inventory_id,
  film_id,
  store_id,
  last_update
FROM inventory
views.description: One-row-per-inventory item (physical copy) with film/store linkage and last_update. Useful for inventory availability, per-store stock counts, and to join to rentals. | Use for: Inventory counts by store/film, joins to rental to compute utilization

views.name: rental_events
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  rental_id,
  rental_date,
  inventory_id,
  customer_id,
  return_date,
  staff_id,
  last_update
FROM rental
views.description: One-row-per-rental event (transactional grain) with timestamps and foreign keys to inventory, customer, and staff. Use this for temporal rental analytics and to join to payments (via rental_id) and inventory. | Use for: Daily/hourly rental volumes, rental duration analysis, late-return detection, joining to payment to compute revenue per rental

views.name: payment_events
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  payment_id,
  customer_id,
  staff_id,
  rental_id,
  amount,
  payment_date,
  last_update
FROM payment
views.description: One-row-per-payment event with amount and date, and links to customer, staff and rental. Use for revenue/time-series and customer-level spend calculations. | Use for: Revenue over time, payments per customer/staff, join to rental to inspect payment completeness

views.name: film_actor_edges
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  fa.actor_id,
  fa.film_id,
  fa.last_update
FROM film_actor fa
views.description: Denormalized one-row-per-film-actor association including actor and film identifiers. Use to join actor attributes onto film-level analyses without multiplying more than necessary. | Use for: Counts of actors per film, actor credits, joining actor names to film lists

views.name: film_category_edges
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  film_id,
  category_id,
  last_update
FROM film_category
views.description: One-row-per-film-category association exposing category linkage for films. Use for category-level aggregates and joins to category names. | Use for: Films per category, category revenue (join through inventory->rental->payment)

views.name: store_location
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.store_id,
  s.manager_staff_id,
  s.address_id,
  a.address,
  a.address2,
  a.district,
  a.city_id,
  c.city,
  c.country_id,
  co.country,
  s.last_update
FROM store s
LEFT JOIN address a ON a.address_id = s.address_id
LEFT JOIN city c ON c.city_id = a.city_id
LEFT JOIN country co ON co.country_id = c.country_id
views.description: Store-level relation joining store to its address, city and country names. One row per store with human-readable location attributes for reporting. | Use for: Store-level reporting, geographic rollups, manager assignments and location-based filtering

views.name: customer_address_profile
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cu.customer_id,
  cu.store_id,
  cu.first_name,
  cu.last_name,
  cu.email,
  cu.address_id,
  a.address,
  a.address2,
  a.district,
  a.city_id,
  ci.city,
  ci.country_id,
  co.country,
  cu.active,
  cu.create_date,
  cu.last_update
FROM customer cu
LEFT JOIN address a ON a.address_id = cu.address_id
LEFT JOIN city ci ON ci.city_id = a.city_id
LEFT JOIN country co ON co.country_id = ci.country_id
views.description: One-row-per-customer including their address, city, and country for geographic analysis of customers. | Use for: Customer geographic distribution, regional revenue, active customer cohorts by location

views.name: payments_by_customer
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  COUNT(payment_id) AS payment_count,
  SUM(amount) AS total_amount
FROM payment
GROUP BY customer_id
views.description: Aggregated payments per customer: total amount and number of payments. Use for customer spend and basic CLV inputs. | Use for: Customer lifetime value estimates, top customers by revenue, segmentation by spend

views.name: rentals_by_inventory
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  inventory_id,
  COUNT(rental_id) AS rental_count,
  AVG(CASE WHEN return_date IS NOT NULL THEN (julianday(return_date) - julianday(rental_date)) ELSE NULL END) AS avg_rental_days
FROM rental
GROUP BY inventory_id
views.description: Aggregates rental counts and average rental duration per inventory item. Useful to measure utilization per physical copy. | Use for: Inventory utilization, average rental duration by copy, identifying underused or overused inventory

views.name: film_revenue_by_film
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  inv.film_id,
  COUNT(p.payment_id) AS payment_count,
  SUM(p.amount) AS total_revenue
FROM payment p
JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id
JOIN inventory inv ON inv.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
GROUP BY inv.film_id
views.description: Aggregate payments mapped to films (via inventory -> rental -> payment) producing total revenue and payment count per film. Useful for film-level revenue ranking. | Use for: Top-grossing films, revenue by film category (join to film_category), revenue per film by store

views.name: latest_payment_per_rental
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.payment_id,
  p.customer_id,
  p.staff_id,
  p.rental_id,
  p.amount,
  p.payment_date,
  p.last_update
FROM (
  SELECT
    payment_id,
    rental_id,
    payment_date,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY rental_id ORDER BY payment_date DESC, payment_id DESC) AS rn
  FROM payment
) rp
JOIN payment p ON p.payment_id = rp.payment_id
WHERE rp.rn = 1
views.description: For each rental_id returns the latest payment (by payment_date). Useful to detect most recent payment tied to a rental or to deduplicate multiple payments per rental. | Use for: Identify last payment per rental, reconcile payments vs rentals, find unpaid rentals

views.name: customer_spend_time_series
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  DATE(payment_date) AS payment_date,
  COUNT(payment_id) AS payment_count,
  SUM(amount) AS total_amount
FROM payment
GROUP BY customer_id, DATE(payment_date)
views.description: Daily aggregated spend per customer (one row per customer per payment_date date). Useful for time-series, cohort retention and rolling metrics. Note: payment_date is truncated to date to create daily buckets. | Use for: Customer daily revenue, cohort time-series, ARPU time series

views.name: film_cast_detail
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  fa.film_id,
  f.title,
  fa.actor_id,
  a.first_name,
  a.last_name,
  fa.last_update
FROM film_actor fa
LEFT JOIN film f ON f.film_id = fa.film_id
LEFT JOIN actor a ON a.actor_id = fa.actor_id
views.description: Film cast details: one row per film-actor with actor names and film title. Useful for film credit displays and actor-based film queries. | Use for: List cast for a film, list films for an actor, actor-film network analysis

views.name: film_category_name
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  fc.film_id,
  fc.category_id,
  c.name AS name,
  fc.last_update
FROM film_category fc
LEFT JOIN category c ON c.category_id = fc.category_id
views.description: One row per film-category including category name, used to attribute films to human-readable categories for reporting. | Use for: Films by category listings, category-level aggregations when combined with revenue or counts
